reason: Full texts of Kulik (PMID 24681342) and Arvind (PMID 38466889) clarify the randomized, treated and transplanted populations, the 30-day biliary endpoint and the five dropout cohorts.

edits.old: 20 patients analyzed. Y90 + sorafenib vs Y90 alone before transplant. 17/20 received a graft. Time to transplant was similar. Biliary complications occurred in 4/8 vs 0/9 recipients. Small randomized safety pilot. Postoperative event counts include only recipients.
edits.new: Y90 plus sorafenib vs Y90 alone. Of 23 randomized, 20 received treatment (10 per arm). 8/10 vs 9/10 received a graft. Time to transplant did not differ significantly (P=0.35). Biliary complications within 30 days occurred in 4/8 vs 0/9 recipients (P=0.029). All 10 sorafenib patients required a permanent dose reduction. The pilot was too small to establish an effect on transplant receipt or survival.

edits.old: 39,819 recipients within Milan. Bridging LRT vs no bridging LRT. Post-transplant recurrence-free survival HR 0.91 (95% CI 0.77–1.08) and overall survival HR 1.09 (0.95–1.24). Recipient outcomes exclude people who dropped out. This cannot establish that bridging is unnecessary during a long wait.
edits.new: 38 retrospective studies of bridging LRT vs no bridging in HCC, focused on patients within Milan criteria (39,819 patients overall). Post-transplant recurrence-free survival HR 0.91 (95% CI 0.77–1.08) and overall survival HR 1.09 (95% CI 0.95–1.24). Five studies reported waitlist dropout (287 bridged, 166 unbridged) and found no significant difference. Selection and differences in waiting time limit inference.

files.old: Recipient studies of bridging versus observation exclude waitlist dropout. Arvind found no clear post-transplant survival difference within Milan.
files.new: Arvind found no clear post-transplant survival difference with bridging LRT in HCC within Milan. Five retrospective cohorts reported dropout (287 bridged, 166 unbridged) and found no significant difference.

files.old: Two small randomized trials found no gain in time to transplant from adding sorafenib to TACE or Y90.
files.new: In two small bridging trials, adding sorafenib to TACE or Y90 showed no clear transplant benefit. In the Y90 pilot, all 10 sorafenib patients needed a dose reduction. Biliary complications within 30 days occurred in 4/8 combination recipients vs 0/9 with Y90 alone.
